extracted.intended_audience: Researchers applying for NIH grants (PIs, early-stage investigators, postdocs seeking K/R awards) and institutional grants staff
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance and standards for managing NIH grant review outcomes, Just-In-Time (JIT) requests, ESI/new-investigator status, paylines, resubmissions, and administrative award processing. Geared toward NIH applicants navigating funding decisions and next-step actions after review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative review and Notice of Award timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Once the GMS is done with the administrative review and drafting the Notice of Award (NoA), the Institute Director must sign off; neither the GMS nor PO control the Director's timing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be patient for the final NoA; the PO/GMS can provide status but cannot force Institute Director signature. The application will be processed for award even if the start date (e.g., April 1) is after that date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start date is an estimate, not an expiration date
rubrics_metrics.description: The April 1 (or other) proposed start date is not an expiration date; the award start date can be after the estimated date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume lack of award if processing extends past the start date; administrators routinely process awards with later effective start dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH allows pre-award spending
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH allows pre-award spending so an institution may set up an account to begin spending against a likely award before the NoA is issued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your institution refuses to set up an account despite confirmation from PO/GMS that the application will receive an award, the PO/GMS cannot override the institution’s decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact of external factors (e.g., COVID-19) on processing efficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH processing efficiency can be affected by external events (staffing changes, school closures, social distancing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect delays and exercise patience; be grateful for positive decisions and courteous to NIH staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning of JIT (Just In Time) requests
rubrics_metrics.description: ICs request JIT information for applications they MIGHT want to fund; receiving a JIT request is a positive signal but not a funding guarantee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit requested JIT materials promptly and coordinate with your PO about whether a brief rebuttal or clarifying information should accompany JIT documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automated JIT timing and cycle dependence
rubrics_metrics.description: Automated JIT requests can appear at different times depending on review cycle (Cycle 2 vs Cycle 3) and IC procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If timing seems odd, confirm cycle and ask your PO whether to begin preparing JIT materials or wait for a tailored request.

rubrics_metrics.name: JIT regulatory approvals requirement (IRB/IACUC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pending or out-of-date IRB/IACUC approvals are not accepted for JIT; appropriate regulatory approvals are required before award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If approvals will take 30–45 days, inform your PO and GMS; ICs have some leeway but near fiscal-year end they may skip applications needing approvals. For phased awards (e.g., R21/R33), submit only the approvals relevant to the phase being funded (e.g., IACUC for R21 now, IRB later for R33).

rubrics_metrics.name: IC discretion and programmatic priorities affect funding beyond payline
rubrics_metrics.description: ICs consider paylines but also apply programmatic discretion; RFAs/PARs/PAS and certain activity codes may not be funded based on score/percentile alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact your PO to understand how programmatic priorities might affect your application's funding likelihood; published paylines vary by IC and mechanism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of 'Pending' status
rubrics_metrics.description: Status changes such as 'Pending' (e.g., 'Pending administrative review') typically indicate that the application has moved to administrative processing and an award is likely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A PO note confirming intent to award can be useful for institutional processes (e.g., tenure review); if unsure, ask the PO or GMS for clarification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Score posting timing is not predictive of score quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Delays in score posting to eRA Commons are driven by SRO/administrative workload and grouping of scores, not the quality or rank of the score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not read into delays; SROs often post scores when all are ready.

rubrics_metrics.name: ESI/new-investigator status: determination and funding-stage update
rubrics_metrics.description: ESI (Early Stage Investigator) status is determined based on status at time of submission and carries through the review process; however, ICs update status at the time of funding decisions to determine the applicable payline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a PI received an award between submission and funding decision, a pending ESI-eligible application may be updated to be ESI-ineligible for funding considerations. Confirm specifics with your PO and consult NIH ESI policy FAQs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Being PI on a multiple-PI application consumes ESI/new-investigator incentive
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are listed as a PI on a multiple-PI (mPI) application and it is funded, you lose ESI/new-investigator status; all PIs on an mPI are treated as PIs for this purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you wish to retain ESI status, be listed as key personnel (co-investigator/collaborator) rather than as a PI on someone else’s mPI application.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH nomenclature: 'Co-PI' vs official roles
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH does not formally recognize the term 'Co-PI' — individuals are either PI, key personnel, or collaborator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Title choices are cosmetic unless listed as PI; avoid being listed as a PI on an mPI if you want to preserve ESI/new-investigator incentives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other Support reporting and percent effort confirmation in JIT
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH requires reporting of Other Support for key personnel in JIT; this includes non-salary support (e.g., supplies) and information on percent effort to confirm availability to conduct the proposed work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report any resources or support that could overlap with proposed work; if a Co-I receives no salary but has funds or obligations elsewhere, NIH will want to know how the person will meet committed effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling potential overlap when mentor/colleague submits related grants
rubrics_metrics.description: If a mentor or collaborator submits an R01 or other application that could overlap with a pending K99/R00 or other award, NIH will require explanations and potential adjustments to avoid paying for the same work twice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss concerns with your PO early; the PO can advocate on your behalf. If your K99/R00 has been peer reviewed and awarded first, later mentor awards should be adjusted to avoid overlap.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to contact the Program Official (PO)
rubrics_metrics.description: Contact your PO after release of the summary statement for advice on resubmission strategy, select pay requests, JIT preparation, and programmatic priority considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include brief bullet responses to reviewer concerns and any new preliminary data when contacting the PO about funding or select pay; the PO can advise whether to submit rebuttal or updated materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission after institutional move
rubrics_metrics.description: You may resubmit an application (A1) from a new institution rather than starting wholly new, but you must address any changes to facilities, space, equipment, research subjects, or institutional resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Update the Facilities & Other Resources and any sections affected by the move; if changing the target NIH Institute, you may need a new submission and PO contact.

rubrics_metrics.name: JIT does not equal funding; prepare for resubmission
rubrics_metrics.description: Receiving a JIT or PO optimism is encouraging but not definitive; prepare to resubmit if on the funding bubble.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use summary statement feedback to plan resubmission, prepare rebuttals where appropriate, and consult the PO about strategy and timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: IC-specific paylines and exceptions (examples and practice)
rubrics_metrics.description: Paylines differ among ICs and mechanisms (e.g., NIDDK examples: established PI R01 ~16th percentile, ESI ~25th), and some solicitations or therapeutic trials may have special consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check IC webpages for current payline policies and ask your PO for specifics; archived funding strategy files can provide context for activity codes without published paylines (e.g., SBIR/STTR).
